justification: Duplicate: master's submission.py already holds module muse_sliding_verify_wgmma_v2b with kernel<TICKET>, the fast one-pass merge_head and the TICKET_ONLY DIAG; both sub-changes were built as specced (base: s2's kernel ported onto c320; the implementer also added a PDL combine, which routed). Measured on the s2b master lineage (log bfb0457c): the ticket-only tail is +1.5-2.7 us, merge_head after the rewrite +17.6-45.0 us, total tk merge +20.3-46.5 us; at B=2..16 the best tk is 40.9 us vs pdl 21.4 and master 24.8. The faster verify_16 / verify_32 sliding rows came from the PDL combine, not this hypothesis. Floors (TASK.md): sliding verify_16 1.9 us, verify_32 3.7 us (weight 46 each); routes ~21.4 us and 29.4-30.3 us, kernel alone 14.6 / 22.4 us, so the remaining gap is the attention kernel, not the merge.
confounders: Already on master (ea24b53c, then 38be4365 / 4e386647): a rerun on master would re-race tk vs pdl, which every import already does; a rerun on the s1 base would differ from the board in everything landed since 10-25.
Pre-attention prologue differs by base (SV32 pre 4.4 vs 6.0 us), so the tk-vs-master ratio would move with the base, not with merge_head.
The bar-1.03 B=17..32 route is marginal (bfb0457c kept master at 1.026x / 1.037x; 4e386647 routed), so sliding verify_32 can move ~3% from gate flips alone.
interference: No companions: tail-vs-merge and tk-vs-pdl are already answered in-run on every master import (af08448e, a76ee9b0, 4e695fa0, 4e386647, bfb0457c).
